questions.q: Why does this lesson build a separate reporting-layer view instead of connecting Power BI directly to fct_orders and dim_customers?
options: fct_orders and dim_customers don't contain any usable data
Power BI cannot connect to tables, only to views, for any reason
The marts layer is built for other dbt models to ref() at full grain with every key; a reporting view drops the columns a report author would never use
There is no difference — connecting directly is equally correct
questions.explain: The lesson applies the same principle the Snowflake capstone used at the warehouse level: a BI tool should query a layer shaped for its own needs, not the full-grain marts tables.

questions.q: What is the purpose of bi_reader_role in this lesson?
options: A least-privilege role scoped only to the reporting schema, used for the Power BI connection instead of the dbt job's own role
A role used only for running dbt itself, never for BI tools
A role with full access to every schema, for convenience
This lesson does not use any roles
questions.explain: Power BI's connection uses bi_reader_role, which is granted SELECT only on the reporting schema — no grant on marts, intermediate, staging, or raw.

questions.q: What does an exposure do in a dbt project, according to this lesson?
options: Deletes models that are no longer used
Replaces the need for schema.yml descriptions
Automatically connects Power BI with no configuration needed
Documents, explicitly, that a downstream report or dashboard depends on specific models, so it shows up as a node in the lineage graph
questions.explain: Once an exposure exists, dbt docs generate shows the report itself as a node depending on the models it references.

questions.q: According to this lesson, where should the Import vs. DirectQuery decision be made?
options: Against the raw schema directly
It must always be Import, never DirectQuery
Against the reporting views, not the marts layer, so a later switch doesn't require re-pointing every report visual at a different table shape
The decision is made automatically by Power BI with no input needed
questions.explain: The lesson notes the decision itself is Snowflake-course material and doesn't change here, but it should target the reporting views specifically.

questions.q: How can you confirm the bi_reader_role boundary is real rather than just assumed?
options: Run SHOW GRANTS on the role and confirm it has no access to marts, staging, or raw schemas
Ask Power BI to report on it automatically
Assume it is correct because the GRANT statements were typed once
There is no way to confirm a role's grants
questions.explain: Just like the Snowflake capstone's RBAC section, the lesson stresses proving the boundary with SHOW GRANTS rather than assuming it's correct.
